description: FoodFlows publishes modelled estimates of how food moves between every pair of counties in the United States, with an interactive map and downloadable data. The datasets come from the Food Flow Model developed by Megan Konar's group at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign with National Science Foundation support, which combines machine learning, network properties, production and consumption statistics, mass-balance constraints and linear programming to disaggregate national freight statistics. The main series covers county-to-county flows in kilograms by food commodity group for 2007, 2012 and 2017 (Karakoc, Wang and Konar 2022, improving Lin et al. 2019), and a companion dataset estimates refrigerated truck flows of meat and prepared foods for 2017 with their carbon dioxide emissions (Wang, Karakoc and Konar 2022). Data are free to download from the website; the licence of the files is not stated on the page, so reuse terms should be checked with the authors or the papers' data statements. Caveats: flows are model estimates, not observed shipments, they cover only the years of the underlying Commodity Flow Survey, and small flows are sensitive to the estimator choices. Simulation uses: building county-scale food supply networks for cascading failure and disruption models, testing how the loss of a production region or a transport link spreads, and linking food flows to road and rail networks. Related records: the Global Food Twin food flows (data-global-food-twin-food-flows) offer a worldwide subnational counterpart.
